headline: Population structure guiding disease modeling, surveillance and intervention decisions
label: Structured Population Disease Modeling
summary: Recent 2026 studies embed granular mobility and surveillance data in structured models to decide where to intervene or sample.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit population structure, spatial or demographic, linked to intervention or surveillance design. The Seoul study uses an age-structured SEIR metapopulation model driven by mobile-phone mobility and reports that targeting adult work flows within clusters reduces COVID-19 spread. The Kenyan malaria study uses a stochastic metapopulation model for western Kenya that jointly captures climate, interventions, immunity and mobility over 2008 to 2019. The Nigerian polio study departs from metapopulation structure: it is a statistical model of time-varying surveillance sensitivity per LGA, validated against 2014 to 2020 WPV1 absence periods. The common element is granular spatial and demographic data used to decide where and whom to model, sample or intervene upon. Because the polio study is not a metapopulation model, the shared thread is structured data rather than a shared model class.
